BG.9.1.context: Krishna opens chapter 9 by promising Arjuna the most secret knowledge.
BG.9.1.english: To you, who do not find fault, I will now reveal this most secret knowledge, together with realised wisdom; knowing it, you will be freed from all that is harmful.

school_notes.note: This is the knowledge of Brahman, the direct means to liberation: 'Vāsudeva is all', 'the self alone is all this'.

This most secret knowledge is devotion in the form of worship (upāsana), together with an understanding of its particular features; it is told to Arjuna because he does not find fault, accepting Krishna's greatness as it is.
This chapter clarifies what chapter 7 taught.

BG.9.2.context: Krishna praises this knowledge as royal, purifying, directly experienced and easy to practise.
BG.9.2.english: It is the king of knowledge, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier, known by direct experience, in keeping with dharma, very easy to practise, and imperishable.

school_notes.note: It is the king of sciences because it shines brightest, and the highest purifier, destroying in a moment the karma of thousands of births.
'Royal knowledge' may also mean the knowledge of the great-minded, who are like kings: broad and deep of mind, and skilled at keeping what should be kept secret.
'Known by direct experience' means that by it Brahman, present within the senses, is known directly; he cites the Upanishad on the one who dwells within the breath.

BG.9.3.context: Krishna warns that without faith in this teaching, people remain in the cycle of death and rebirth.
BG.9.3.english: People who have no faith in this dharma, scorcher of enemies, do not reach me but return to the path of death and worldly existence.

school_notes.note: Without faith in this knowledge of the self and its fruit, unbelievers who see only the body as the self return to the path of mortal existence.
This dharma is worship of me; those without faith in it do not reach me and remain on the path of death and rebirth.

BG.9.4.context: Krishna begins a paradox: all beings rest in him, yet he is not contained in them (9.4-9.6).
BG.9.4.english: All this world is pervaded by me in my unmanifest form. All beings dwell in me, but I do not dwell in them.

school_notes.note: My supreme nature, beyond the reach of the senses, pervades the world; beings dwell in me, the unmanifest, but I am not in them as something contained.
I pervade this whole world, unseen, as its inner controller, to sustain and govern it, as the Upanishad says: 'who dwells in the earth, whom the earth does not know'.
If he pervades everything, why is he not seen? Because his form is unmanifest.

BG.9.5.context: Krishna completes the paradox, calling it a sign of his divine power.
BG.9.5.english: And yet beings do not dwell in me: see my divine power! My self sustains all beings and brings them into being, yet does not dwell in them.

school_notes.note: The self is unattached, as the Upanishad says: 'it is unattached, it clings to nothing'. This is my divine yoga.
Beings do not rest in me as water rests in a pot; I hold them by my will alone. I support all beings, yet receive no support from them.
They are in him, yet not in contact with him the way things touch the earth; his very body sustains beings.

BG.9.6.context: Krishna gives the image of wind in space to explain how beings rest in him.
BG.9.6.english: As the mighty wind, moving everywhere, always rests in space, so all beings rest in me: understand this.

school_notes.note: As wind moves within space without touching it, so beings rest in me, all-pervading like space, without contact.
As a great wind moves everywhere in space with no support, held only by me, so all beings rest in me and are held by me.
Wind resting in space does not take on the qualities of space.

BG.9.7.context: Krishna describes the cycle of creation and dissolution that he governs (9.7-9.10).
BG.9.7.english: At the end of a cosmic age, son of Kunti, all beings return to my nature; at the beginning of an age, I send them forth again.

school_notes.note: At dissolution all beings enter my lower, three-guna nature; at creation I send them forth again as before.
At the end of Brahmā's life, by my will, beings enter my prakṛti, which is my body and is called 'darkness'; at the start of the next age I send them forth again, as Manu says.

BG.9.8.context: Krishna says beings arise again and again, carried by the power of nature that he governs.
BG.9.8.english: Taking hold of my own nature, I send forth again and again this whole multitude of beings, helpless under the power of nature.

school_notes.note: Mastering my own prakṛti, I send forth again and again the whole host of beings, made helpless by ignorance and other faults, under the sway of their own nature.
Shaping my prakṛti eightfold, I send forth the four kinds of beings (gods, animals, humans and plants), helpless under the spell of prakṛti.
He leans on prakṛti the way a capable person might lean on a stick while walking, in play.

BG.9.9.context: Krishna says he creates without being bound, like a detached witness.
BG.9.9.english: These actions do not bind me, Arjuna, for I sit as if indifferent, unattached to these actions.

school_notes.note: The acts that cause the unequal creation of beings do not bind me, for I sit like one unconcerned, changeless and without attachment to their fruit.
Unequal creation does not make me cruel or partial, since the differences come from beings' own past karma, as the Brahma Sūtra says.
'As if indifferent', but not truly indifferent: whatever exists exists by his favour and ceases by his neglect, as the Bhāgavata says.

BG.9.10.context: Krishna explains that nature creates the world under his oversight.
BG.9.10.english: Under my supervision, nature gives birth to all that moves and does not move; because of this, son of Kunti, the world turns.

school_notes.note: With me as witness, unchanging awareness, my māyā produces the moving and unmoving world, as the Upanishad says: 'the one God hidden in all beings'.
Overseen by me, whose will is always fulfilled, my prakṛti brings forth the world according to beings' karma; this shows my lordship and my freedom from cruelty.
If he is 'as if indifferent', does prakṛti produce by itself? No: I alone oversee and bring about prakṛti's production.

BG.9.11.context: Krishna laments that people mistake him in human form for an ordinary person (9.11-9.12).
BG.9.11.english: Fools disregard me when I take on a human body, not knowing my higher nature as the great Lord of all beings.

school_notes.note: The undiscerning look down on me acting in a human body, not knowing my supreme nature, subtler than space, the great Lord of beings.
Deluded by their own sins, they take me, who out of supreme compassion took a human body so that all could approach me, for an ordinary human being.
'Human body' means a body the deluded take to be human, not a human form in truth.

BG.9.12.context: Krishna describes the emptiness of a life that rejects the divine.
BG.9.12.english: Their hopes in vain, their actions in vain, their knowledge in vain, senseless, they take on the deluding nature of rakshasas and asuras.

school_notes.note: Because they disregard the Lord, their own self, even their rites such as the fire offering bear no fruit, and their knowledge is futile.
Taking on the deluding nature that hides my supreme compassion in human form, their hopes, efforts and knowledge all bear no fruit.
Nothing that those hostile to the Lord hope for is gained, and their rites and knowledge are futile.

BG.9.13.context: Krishna contrasts those with a divine nature, who worship him wholeheartedly (9.13-9.15).
BG.9.13.english: But great souls, son of Pritha, who take on the divine nature, worship me with undivided minds, knowing me as the imperishable source of beings.

school_notes.note: Great souls take on the divine nature, marked by calm, self-control, compassion and faith, and worship me with undivided mind.
Those whose sins are destroyed by taking refuge in me take on the divine nature and, knowing me as come down in human form to protect the good, worship me with undivided mind.
These are the divine beings, set against those who are hostile to the Lord.

BG.9.14.context: Krishna describes the devotion of great souls: praise, effort and reverence.
BG.9.14.english: Always singing my praise, striving with firm resolve, and bowing to me in devotion, they worship me, ever disciplined.

school_notes.note: They always praise me, strive through restraint of the senses, self-control, compassion and non-violence, and bow to me, the Lord within the heart.
Unable to live a moment without praising me, their hair standing on end and voices choked with joy, they constantly chant names such as Rāma, Nārāyaṇa, Krishna and Vāsudeva.

BG.9.15.context: Krishna describes others who worship him through knowledge, in unity and in diversity.
BG.9.15.english: Others, offering the sacrifice of knowledge, worship me as the One, as distinct, and in many ways, as the one whose face is everywhere.

school_notes.note: Some worship with the knowledge of oneness, seeing the one supreme Brahman; others as distinct, seeing the Lord as other than themselves; others in many forms.
They worship me as one: Vāsudeva, who exists as the whole world in its many forms, with all of it as his body.
As one: the one Nārāyaṇa present everywhere; as distinct: as different from everything else; in many ways: in his many forms, as the Sanatsujāta describes.

BG.9.16.context: Krishna identifies himself with every element of sacred ritual (9.16-9.19).
BG.9.16.english: I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the offering to the ancestors, I am the healing herb; I am the sacred chant, I am the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering.

school_notes.note: I am the Vedic rite and the sacrifice of tradition, the food offered to the ancestors, and the grain that all beings eat.
I am rites such as the Jyotiṣṭoma, the great sacrifice, the offering that nourishes the ancestors; every element of the rite is me.
Sacrifice is the giving up of a substance for a deity, as a lexicon defines it.

BG.9.17.context: Krishna calls himself the father, mother and sustainer of the world, and the essence of the Vedas.
BG.9.17.english: I am the father of this world, its mother, its sustainer and its grandfather; I am what is to be known, the purifier, the syllable Om, and the Rig, Sama and Yajur Vedas.

school_notes.note: Father as the one who begets, mother as the one who bears, sustainer as the one who apportions the fruits of karma, and grandfather as the father's father.
I am present as the father, mother, sustainer and grandfather of all beings; whatever is purifying and knowable is me.

BG.9.18.context: Krishna names himself as goal, refuge and friend of all beings.
BG.9.18.english: I am the goal, the support, the lord, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend; the origin, the dissolution and the ground, the treasure-house and the imperishable seed.

school_notes.note: The refuge, who removes the suffering of those who come to him; the friend, who helps without expecting anything in return.
'Refuge' is the conscious being one turns to, who brings what is wanted and keeps away what is not; 'friend' is the one who wishes one well.
'Goal' is what seekers of liberation reach; 'witness' is the one who sees directly, as the Veda says.

BG.9.19.context: Krishna says he is both the forces that sustain life and those that end it.
BG.9.19.english: I give heat; I hold back the rain and send it forth. I am immortality and also death, being and non-being, Arjuna.

school_notes.note: As the sun, I give heat with some rays and send rain with others; I am immortality for the gods and death for mortals.
As fire and sun I give heat, hold back rain in summer and release it in the rains; I am both what makes the world live and what makes it die.
'Being' is the manifest effect, 'non-being' the unmanifest cause.

BG.9.20.context: Krishna describes ritualists who seek heaven: their reward is real but temporary (9.20-9.21).
BG.9.20.english: Those who know the three Vedas, who drink the soma and are cleansed of sin, worship me with sacrifices and pray for the way to heaven; reaching the holy world of the lord of the gods, they enjoy the divine pleasures of the gods in heaven.

school_notes.note: Knowers of the three Vedas, purified by the soma they drink, worship me in the form of the Vasus and other gods and pray to go to heaven.
These are devoted only to the three Vedas, not to their culmination, the Vedānta; those devoted to Vedānta worship me through praise and the sacrifice of knowledge.
Shows that worshipping him is better than worshipping other gods.

BG.9.21.context: Krishna says heavenly rewards run out, returning their seekers to the cycle of birth.
BG.9.21.english: Having enjoyed that vast heavenly world, they return to the world of mortals when their merit is spent; following the dharma of the three Vedas and wanting pleasures, they come and go.

school_notes.note: Following only the rites of the three Vedas and wanting pleasures, they go and come back.
Lacking the knowledge established in Vedānta and seeking heaven through Vedic rites alone, they enjoy small, unstable pleasures and return again and again.

BG.9.22.context: Krishna promises to provide for and protect those devoted to him alone.
BG.9.22.english: Those who think of no one else and worship me, always disciplined, I bring them what they lack and protect what they have.

school_notes.note: For renunciants who know the supreme God as their own self and worship him constantly, I provide what they lack and protect what they have.
For those who cannot live without thinking of me and worship me fully, I myself bring about their union with me, from which there is no return, and keep it secure.
'Thinking of no one else' means thinking of nothing other than him, as the Gautama supplements say.

BG.9.23.context: Krishna says worship of other gods ultimately reaches him, though without true understanding (9.23-9.25).
BG.9.23.english: Even those devoted to other gods, who worship them with faith, are really worshipping me, son of Kunti, though not in the proper way.

school_notes.note: Those devoted to other gods worship me, but 'not in the proper way', which means out of ignorance.
Worshippers of Indra and others really worship me, since all are my body and their names ultimately refer to me; but they do not know this.
Otherwise 'I am the ritual' (9.16) would be untrue.

BG.9.24.context: Krishna explains why such worship falls short: he is the real recipient of every sacrifice.
BG.9.24.english: For I am the enjoyer and the lord of all sacrifices; but they do not know me as I truly am, and so they fall.

school_notes.note: I am the enjoyer of all sacrifices as their deity, and their lord, as 8.4 said; not knowing me truly, they worship wrongly and fall.
How remarkable that within the same rite, a mere difference of intention makes some gain small, fleeting fruits and others the boundless joy of reaching the Supreme Person.
Gives the reason why worship is properly directed to him.

BG.9.25.context: Krishna says people reach whatever they devote themselves to.
BG.9.25.english: Those devoted to the gods go to the gods; those devoted to the ancestors go to the ancestors; those who worship spirits go to the spirits; and those who worship me come to me.

school_notes.note: Those devoted to the gods reach the gods; those devoted to ancestral rites reach the ancestors; worshippers of spirits reach the spirits; my worshippers reach me.
'Devoted' here means having the intention: those who resolve to worship Indra and the rest reach them.

BG.9.26.context: Krishna says even the simplest offering, given with love, is accepted by him.
BG.9.26.english: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from one whose heart is pure, I accept.

school_notes.note: Whoever offers me a leaf, flower, fruit or water with devotion, I accept it from that person of pure mind.
Even something anyone can obtain, a leaf or a flower, offered by one who out of love cannot live without giving it, I receive as if it were something I had never had.
Answers the worry that the weak cannot worship one so great: he is pleased by devotion alone; but offering what is not permitted is a fault.

BG.9.27.context: Krishna teaches turning every part of life into an offering (9.27-9.28).
BG.9.27.english: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer in sacrifice, whatever you give, whatever austerity you practise, son of Kunti, do it as an offering to me.

school_notes.note: Whatever you do, whatever you eat, offer, give to brahmins and others, or practise as austerity, do it as an offering to me.
Offer all ordinary and Vedic actions to me, giving up the sense of being their doer and enjoyer.

BG.9.28.context: Krishna says offering every act to him frees one from karma's bonds.
BG.9.28.english: In this way you will be freed from the bonds of action, with their good and bad results; with your self joined in the yoga of renunciation, you will be set free and come to me.

school_notes.note: Offering everything to me frees you from actions with good and bad results; this offering is called the yoga of renunciation.
Knowing yourself as existing for me and governed by me, and all action as my worship, you will be freed from the endless bonds of past karma and come to me.

BG.9.29.context: Krishna says he is impartial to all, yet especially close to those who love him.
BG.9.29.english: I am the same to all beings; no one is hateful to me and no one is dear. But those who worship me with devotion are in me, and I am in them.

school_notes.note: Like fire, which takes away the cold only for those who come near it, I favour my devotees and not others; they are in me by their very nature.
Among all beings, however high or low by birth, form, nature or knowledge, I am equally the refuge; no one is rejected as too low to approach me.
Those who worship me are under my care and I am under theirs, as the Paiṅgi supplements say.

BG.9.30.context: Krishna says devotion counts for more than a person's past conduct (9.30-9.31).
BG.9.30.english: Even if a person of very bad conduct worships me with undivided devotion, they should be regarded as good, for they have resolved rightly.

school_notes.note: Even one of very bad conduct who worships me alone should be considered good, since their resolve is right.
Even one who has broken the conduct proper to their birth, if they worship me for its own sake, is to be honoured as a foremost Vaiṣṇava, equal to those described before.
A devotee is rarely of very bad conduct; but if, by great merit, such a person becomes a devotee, they should be considered good.

BG.9.31.context: Krishna promises that his devotee is never lost.
BG.9.31.english: They quickly become righteous and attain lasting peace. Know this for certain, son of Kunti: my devotee never perishes.

school_notes.note: Make this firm promise, Arjuna: my devotee, whose inner self is offered to me, never perishes.
With sins removed by devotion and rajas and tamas uprooted, they quickly become wholly given to worship and reach lasting peace.
Such complete devotion arises in gods and their portions; he cites the Śāṇḍilya branch of the Sāmaveda.

BG.9.32.context: Krishna says the highest goal is open to all who take refuge in him, naming groups ranked low in his society.
BG.9.32.english: For those who take refuge in me, son of Pritha, even those of sinful birth, women, vaishyas and shudras, they too reach the highest goal.

school_notes.note: 'Of sinful birth': who are they? Women, vaishyas and shudras; they too reach the highest goal.
Women, vaishyas and shudras, though of sinful birth, reach the highest goal by taking refuge in me.

BG.9.33.context: Krishna urges Arjuna, a royal sage, to worship him while living in this fleeting world.
BG.9.33.english: How much more, then, holy brahmins and devoted royal sages! Having come to this impermanent, joyless world, worship me.

school_notes.note: If even they reach it, how much more brahmins of meritorious birth and royal sages. Having gained a human birth, rare and the means to life's goal, in this fleeting, joyless world, worship me.
How much more brahmins of meritorious birth and royal sages; so you, a royal sage, living in this unstable world struck by threefold suffering, should worship me.

BG.9.34.context: Krishna closes chapter 9 with a call to wholehearted devotion, repeated at 18.65.
BG.9.34.english: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, worship me, bow down to me. Disciplining yourself in this way, with me as your goal, you will come to me.

school_notes.note: Let your mind be on me, Vāsudeva; be my devotee, worship me and bow to me; absorbed in this way, with me as your highest goal, you will reach me, the self of all beings.
Fix your mind on me, the Lord of all, free of every flaw and full of every auspicious quality, with eyes like lotus petals, dark as a rain cloud and radiant as a thousand suns.
